headline: Last session: Sensex surged nearly 900 points as IT and FMCG stocks recovered strongly

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 12 October.

why: Sensex recovered nearly 900 points in the last trading session led by a broad rally in IT and FMCG stocks.
TCS shares jumped significantly, leading a 3% surge in the IT sector index.
Persistent selling pressure remains a concern as FIIs dumped Indian equities for eight straight weeks.
Earlier market declines were triggered by rising oil prices topping $104 and a rate hike by the RBI.
whatHappening: On the last trading day, Sensex closed nearly 900 points higher and Nifty moved above 22,500.
DMart reported its Q2 results showing a consolidated profit rise of nearly 9% YoY to Rs 743 crore on an 18% revenue jump.
The IT sector jumped 3% while FMCG indices gained over 2% on Friday.
Earlier in the week on Thursday, Indian benchmarks suffered a massive drop of over 1,000 points.
summary:
On the last trading day, Indian benchmark indices rebounded strongly with Sensex surging nearly 900 points and Nifty closing above 22,500.
The gains were powered by a rally in IT stocks led by TCS alongside gains in the FMCG sector.
Meanwhile, DMart posted a nearly 9% YoY increase in Q2 net profit to Rs 743 crore on strong revenue growth.
